newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman's Sultan decrees the first constitution.
newsitem.headline: Oman's Sultan decrees the first constitution.

text.p: Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said on Wednesday issued a decree laying out the country's first written constitution and preparing the framework for his succession.
The decree, issued by the official Omani news agency, said the ruling family should decide on a male successor from the bin Said family three days after "the post of the Sultan becomes vacant".
If they fail to agree "then the defence council will confirm the successor" recommended by Sultan Qaboos in a letter to the family, it said.
Sultan Qaboos, 56, has had no heir apparent since he took over from his father in 1970. He is not married.
Diplomats said the decree aimed at avoiding a power vacuum or internal struggle after his death.
The decree laid out what it called Oman's "basic law", which diplomats said was the country's first written constitution.
One of its items said succession in Oman is hereditary.
It said Oman was an independent Arab country. Islam was its religion and Arabic its language. The economy is based on free market principles.

Oman, with a population of over two million, is a small independent oil producer and a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council which also groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
